mentl/f11daa8:
The seed's float support was a fake: every TFloat binop intercepted to
(drop)(drop)(i32.const 0), every literal floored, every float fn
(param i32). In m2 that meant f / 10.0 was integer div-by-zero and
float_floor_log10 recursed to stack exhaustion the moment the wheel's
emit rendered any float literal — the root under all three +rt rungs.

The substrate, landed across three agent cycles and ratcheted at every
step: f64 literals emitted from $mk_TFloat's raw decimal text; f64
add/sub/mul/div/neg and comparisons; float_of_int / float_to_int
conversions; f64-typed params, locals, and results; inline-typed
call_indirect where floats ride (all-i32 calls byte-identical);
(if (result f64)) and match-arm f64 threading (the fix that made
float_at genuine); param widths computed ONCE and fed to both the
signature and the body ledger (the divergence that had the same param
f64 in the signature and i32 at its own binop); a tail call's result
typed as the ENCLOSING fn's result, the WASM invariant, not the
callee's prediction; LMatch in the width predictor reading the same
arm scan emit uses; conversion elided when the operand's emitted
width already matches.

Where an f64 value crosses a boundary the seed cannot yet type —
heap aggregates (27 sites), the fixed-i32 evidence dispatch (2), and
three DSP op-lambdas — the emit is a LOUD (unreachable) floor with a
censused marker, never a silent zero. The wheel never yields: its
TFloatLit(Float) stays correct; the seed gains capability.

Gates: seed builds; verify 35 micros green including the new
float-gate=3 (real f64 math through the seed — the floored seed gave
0); m2.wat assembles at ZERO wat2wasm errors (the arc's ladder:
159 -> 70 -> 10 -> 0); all five integer rungs hold. The three +rt
rungs now trap at !lex_from — the heap-crossing floor at the lexer's
TFloatLit variant payload — the named next face
(Hb.seed.f64-in-heap-record), reached honestly: the trap marched
through the fake into the real remaining substrate.
